title: model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama / Mistral / Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Performance: model-specific kernel selection + scheduler heuristics reduce P99 and token cost for Llama/Mistral/Qwen. Stability: KV cache alignment fixes for Qwen edge cases. Ops: rollout flags for gradual canary and automatic fallback to generic kernels.
description: Context: We see recurring model-specific performance regressions due to suboptimal kernel choices, schedule mispredictions, and subtle KV cache layout differences across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen model families. This PR implements targeted runtime optimizations and feature flags to safely roll them out. Motivation: reduce per-token latency and unit cost while avoiding regressions for smaller sequences and multi-model fleets. Summary of changes: 1) Kernel selection: introduced a short-path decision tree that prefers reduced-memory GEMM kernels for MQA/GQA patterns detected in Qwen and Llama derivatives; added microbenchmarks to pick between fused attention kernels and split-k implementations based on sequence length histogram. 2) Scheduler heuristics: updated continuous batching heuristic to prefer keeping hot KV-cached sessions on dedicated lanes during bursts, lowering token tail latency for chat workloads. 3) KV cache alignment fixes: corrected Qwen-specific KV packing offsets that could cause 8-byte misalignment on some quantized layouts (observed as occasional corrupt outputs in long-context workloads). 4) GQA/MQA tuning: tuned group-quantization aggregation in the runtime to avoid cross-group accumulation hotspots; added fast-path for non-divisible group sizes used by some Llama checkpoints. 5) Telemetry and rollout: new metrics (kernel_choice, scheduler_lane, kv_alignment_mismatch) and runtime flags (flags.runtime.model_quirks_v1) with canary-by-customer rollout. Benchmarks: end-to-end tests on rtx-8000-like and A100 fleets show median token latency down 8-12% and P99 down 15-20% on interactive chat traces for targeted models; cost-per-token reduces by ~6% due to batching + kernel improvements. Testing: unit tests for packing/packing invariants, integration tests with synthetic long-context traces, and a staged canary across Dedicated clusters. Rollout plan: canary 1% of traffic, monitor kernel_choice and kv_alignment_mismatch for 48h, expand to 25% after no regressions for 72h, then global. Related work: builds on ENG-3810 (continuous-batching refactor) and ENG-3955 (kv cache schema v2). Checklist: [x] unit tests added, [x] integration tests added, [x] telemetry added, [x] feature flag guarded, [ ] docs updated (follow-up PR). Linear/Jira: ENG-4123, ENG-4192. Notes: avoided touching scheduler preemption logic in this change to minimize blast radius; follow-up will evaluate preemption + lane consolidation for GPU packing improvements.
